etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English, from Middle French immun, from Latin immūnis (“exempt from public service”), from in- (“not”) + mūnus (“service”).

quote.citation: 1922, Michael Arlen, “2/9/1”, in “Piracy”: A Romantic Chronicle of These Days‎[1]:
quote.text: He had always been remarkably immune from such little ailments, and had only once in his life been ill, of a vicious pneumonia long ago at school. He hadn't the faintest idea what to with a cold in the head, he just took quinine and continued to blow his nose.

quote.citation: 2019 September 3, David Karpf, “Bret Stephens Compared Me to a Nazi Propagandist in the New York Times. It Proved My Point.”, in Esquire‎[2]:
quote.text: Bret Stephens believed that, by virtue of his comfortable position at the New York Times, he ought to be immune from insult or criticism.

definitions.definition: (medicine, usually with "to") Protected by inoculation, or due to innate resistance to pathogens.

quote.citation: 1959 June, “The opening of the Colchester-Walton-Clacton electrification”, in Trains Illustrated, page 306:
quote.text: [...] most of the original electrical signalling equipment has had to be replaced by apparatus immune to 50-cycle currents.

quote.citation: 2013 May-June, Katrina G. Claw, “Rapid Evolution in Eggs and Sperm”, in American Scientist, volume 101, number 3:
quote.text: Many genes with reproductive roles also have antibacterial and immune functions, which indicate that the threat of microbial attack on the sperm or egg may be a major influence on rapid evolution during reproduction.

definitions.definition: (epidemiology) A person who is not susceptible to infection by a particular disease

quote.citation: 1965, Rene J. Dubos, James G. Hirsch, editors, Bacterial and Mycotic Infections of Man‎[3], page 742:
quote.text: Susceptibles effectively exposed to cases become cases in the next time period; cases recovering from the infection accumulate as immunes.
In the seventies those who met me did not know / Of the vision / That immuned me from the chillings of mis-prision  […]

quote.citation: 1905, American Veterinary Medical Association, Journal, volume 29, page 42:
quote.text: The utilization of such milk will, however, necessitate an adaptable milk preservation method, through which the immuning agents will not be destroyed or diminished.
